nodes.label: Local Overridability (Invariant 1 / Leitprinzip 7)
nodes.rationale: All reputation/blocking parameters must remain locally overridable by the operator. Lists are aids, not law. Prevents centralisation of control and preserves operator sovereignty.

nodes.label: IPs as Personal Data (Invariant 2 / spec §9)
nodes.rationale: IPs are cleartext on the wire and treated as personal data under GDPR. Hashing is not anonymisation. Lawful basis is legitimate interest plus decay as automatic deletion.

nodes.label: Local-Only Whitelist Never Federated (Invariant 3 / spec §6.2)
nodes.rationale: Own IP, gateway, DNS, Docker ranges are scope: local-only and must never appear in gossip or any pkg/proto type. Prevents operator topology leakage.

nodes.label: O(1) Enforcement via ipset/nftables (Invariant 4 / spec §11.3)
nodes.rationale: Use ipset/nftables sets for O(1) membership checks. Never generate one firewall rule per IP as that is O(n) per packet and melts under attack.

nodes.label: Asymmetric Trust Decay (Invariant 5 / spec §4.3)
nodes.rationale: Trust rises slowly and falls fast. This asymmetry is a core anti-poisoning mechanism. Any decay constant or corroboration change must preserve this.

nodes.label: Trust Anchors Locally Removable (Invariant 6 / spec §5.1)
nodes.rationale: Project-provided trust anchors are a default, never mandatory. An irremovable anchor re-centralises the system.

nodes.label: Security-Critical Paths (Invariant 7)
nodes.rationale: internal/enforce and scripts/install/ are security-critical. Extra review and conservative defaults are required. Explicit operator confirmation before writing.

nodes.label: Three-Plane Architecture (Data / Control / Observability)
nodes.rationale: Data plane (enforce) is small and isolated because it is security-critical. Control plane handles reputation/trust/transport. Observability is opt-in, default OFF — never mandatory.

nodes.label: Sybil Resistance via Diversity Weighting
nodes.rationale: Diversity weighting collapses reporters from same ASN/subnet toward ~1 effective vote. N independent ASNs/countries required, not N nodes.

nodes.label: Reputation Decay (TTL as GDPR Deletion)
nodes.rationale: BadgerDB TTL drives reputation decay. Decay doubles as GDPR storage-limitation (Art. 6(1)(f), Recital 49). Decay-as-deletion avoids explicit erasure obligations.

nodes.label: Federation Import Discount
nodes.rationale: Foreign consensus counts less than own (import_discount: 0.5). Prevents a single subnet from dominating another via federation. Spec §5.2.

nodes.label: SchemaVersion Bump on Wire Changes
nodes.rationale: Any field add/remove/semantic change requires bumping SchemaVersion and a CHANGELOG entry. Mixed-version networks are normal; nodes must tolerate unknown/missing optional fields.

nodes.label: Ground-Truth Anchors (Honeypots / Spamtraps)
nodes.rationale: Honeypots and spamtraps are ground-truth sources: any connection is malicious by definition. Wired as high-weight trust anchors via internal/trust, not ordinary low-trust reporters (spec §4.1, §6.1).

nodes.label: Non-Invasive Mailcow Integration Pattern
nodes.rationale: Uses docker-compose.override.yml so Mailcow's own files are untouched and upgrades remain safe. Mirrors JoeRu/Mailcow-Crowdsec-Override pattern.

nodes.label: OriginTrace / SubnetID Provenance
nodes.rationale: OriginTrace and SubnetID prevent federation feedback loops (double-counting). Must not be dropped in transforms. Spec §5.2, problem K.
